tooling: Jupyter; compute units on the paid tiers: Colab Pro includes 100 compute units per month and Colab Pro+ includes 600 per month, and compute units expire after 90 days
chaining: none for a scheduled workload: the ceiling is discretionary on every tier

limits.value: compute units are a separate currency and their consumption is not published
paid users whose compute units are exhausted revert to the free tier policies

limits_note: a documented absence of limits is a discretionary throttle, not a quota, and it does not become one when paid for
notes: The paid tiers do not publish a quota either. A workload that needs a published ceiling cannot be scheduled here at any price, which is a stronger statement than 'the free tier is small'.

free_tier.stated: no published quota on any tier: Colab states its limits vary and are not published, and paid tiers fall back to the free policies when compute units are exhausted
free_tier.notes: a paid tier whose limits are unpublished cannot be budgeted; the GPU and TPU types are not named and vary over time, GPU access on the free tier is heavily restricted, and a free-tier notebook runs at most 12 hours depending on availability

retention.stated: a VM is deleted when idle and has a maximum lifetime enforced by the service

identity_cost.detail: a paid tier requires a payment, and the paid offerings are only available in the countries that the pricing page lists (the list starts: United States of America, Canada, Brazil, France, Germany, India, Japan)

evidence.proved: Colab does not publish its limits because they vary over time; paid users revert to free-tier policies when units run out
Colab states that it does not publish its usage limits, so no free GPU hour quota, weekly cap or card type is stated
evidence.quote: Colab does not publish these limits, in part because they can vary over time.

evidence.proved: a paid user with no compute units left falls back to the free-tier policies
evidence.quote: Paid users whose compute unit balance is exhausted will revert to the free-of-charge tier policies and restrictions until the balance is increased.

evidence.proved: free-tier GPU access is heavily restricted and no GPU model or hour count is published
evidence.quote: In the version of Colab that is free of charge, access to expensive resources like GPUs is heavily restricted.

evidence.proved: a free-tier notebook runs at most 12 hours, depending on availability and usage
evidence.quote: In the version of Colab that is free of charge notebooks can run for at most 12 hours, depending on availability and your usage patterns.

evidence.proved: Colab Pro+ totals 600 compute units per month; the same page lists 100 per month for Pro and 90-day expiry
evidence.quote: An additional 500 compute units per month, totaling 600 compute units per month.

evidence.proved: paid Colab plans are sold only in a listed set of countries
evidence.quote: For now, the Colab paid offerings are only available in the following countries: United States of America, Canada, Brazil, France, Germany, India, Japan

session_cap.note: free tier and Pro: at most 12 hours depending on availability; Pro+ background execution up to 24 hours; idle timeout not published

binding_note: the compute-unit allowance binds and the policies behind it are unpublished, so there is no ceiling to schedule against
